topic: Pale Blue Dot: Voyager 1's photo of Earth (1990)
claim: On Feb. 14, 1990 Voyager 1, about 6 billion km from the Sun, photographed Earth as a crescent only 0.12 pixels wide, in 60 frames of the first family portrait of the solar system; the image inspired Carl Sagan's book Pale Blue Dot.

beats.caption: THIS DOT IS YOU
beats.vo: That tiny dot is all of us.

beats.caption: FEBRUARY 14, 1990
beats.vo: On February fourteenth, nineteen ninety, Voyager 1 was about six billion kilometers from the Sun.

beats.caption: 60 FRAMES
beats.vo: From there, it took sixty frames, the first family portrait of the solar system.

beats.caption: LESS THAN ONE PIXEL
beats.vo: Earth fills less than one pixel. Just a crescent, point one two of a pixel wide.

beats.caption: A BEAM OF LIGHT
beats.vo: A beam of scattered sunlight runs right through it.

beats.caption: PALE BLUE DOT
beats.vo: Carl Sagan named his book after it. Look again at that dot. That's here. That's home. That's us.

sources.text: NASA Science, Voyager 1's Pale Blue Dot (Feb. 14, 1990; 3.7 billion miles / 6 billion km from the Sun): https://science.nasa.gov/resource/voyager-1s-pale-blue-dot/
NASA/JPL Photojournal PIA00452 (60 frames; Earth a crescent 0.12 pixels; scattered light ray): https://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00452
